sentences.text: This video can not be played Aerial footage shows wheeled robot near white vans Five men have been arrested on suspicion of explosive and terrorism offences after a major incident was declared at an airbase in the west of England.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Bomb disposal teams have been examining a number of vehicles near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire and dozens of homes in the surrounding area have been evacuated.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Here is a summary of what we know so far.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Gloucestershire Police said they received a call about "three suspicious vehicles" travelling towards RAF Fairford at 00:45 BST on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Five men were later arrested by its officers near Whelford, a village around two miles (3.2km) south-east of the base.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: A bomb disposal team was also deployed to the village to examine a number of vehicles, police said, around which a 400m (1,312ft) cordon is in place.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Aerial pictures showed a remote-controlled robot approaching two stationary white vans in a wooded area, though its use has not been confirmed by police.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Counter Terrorism Policing (CTP) is leading the investigation into the incident.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The BBC understands the operation was not intelligence led.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: RAF Fairford is located in the Cotswolds, about four miles (6.4km) south of the town of Fairford, which sits along the River Coln.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The base shares a long history with the American military, and has recently been used by US warplanes as a staging post for defensive strikes on Iran.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: There has been a large emergency service presence in the area since the early hours of Sunday, which Gloucestershire Police Temporary Chief Constable Maggie Blyth said would remain over the next few days.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Blyth told a news conference on Sunday evening that the force would continue to assist CTP and liaise with other national partners.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: She also said she would leave any declaration of a "terrorist incident" to CTP.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: What we know about the counter-terrorism operation near RAF Fairford Five men were initially detained on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: They were then further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The men, who remain in custody, have not been named.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Police have not said where they are being held.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Suspects arrested under the Terrorism Act 2000 can be detained for up to 14 days without charge, compared to the 24-hour limit for standard arrests without an extension application.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Asked whether police were seeking other individuals in connection with the incident, Blyth said she believed the matter was "contained".
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump said those arrested were "looking to do big damage", adding: "We had them under view for a long time, and we got them." This image has been circulating following the arrests of five men near RAF Fairford BBC Your Voice has received an image purporting to show the moment five men were arrested.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: It showed detained men in Whelford, about 350m (1,148ft) from runway access at Crash Gate 6A at RAF Fairford.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The BBC has been unable to verify the original source but BBC Verify has geolocated the image and confirmed it appeared to be authentic.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: A resident who called 999 to report the three white vans in Whelford village said it was "pure luck" that she spotted the vehicles.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme the woman, who wishes to remain anonymous, said she arrived home to find the driveway and road blocked and saw a "large group of hooded and masked men".
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: "When they saw me they ran ahead of me - some into the field and some towards the neighbouring village of Kempsford.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: I then realised that something highly unusual was taking place," she added.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The woman told the programme she called the Ministry of Defence police at RAF Fairford but received no answer.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: She then rang 999 at 01:36 BST and said "within 10 minutes the village was full of armed police".
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: "I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had." "I am absolutely staggered that it was left to me as a member of the public to see and report this," she said.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: "Someone really dropped the ball on this." Another resident described the moment he said he saw police apprehend the suspects.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Jeff - who did not give his surname - told the BBC he heard "shouting outside his front door", although he could not be sure where it came from.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: He said he then looked out of his window and saw "people being held by police outside".
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Gloucestershire Police said displaced residents have been told they will not be able to return to their homes on Sunday night.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Overnight accommodation will be found by Cotswold District Council for those affected who are unable to stay with family and friends, according to Deputy Chief Executive David Stanley.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Eighty-five households were evacuated following the incident and urged to shelter at a nearby leisure centre.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Several people have told the BBC they were woken by police in the early hours of Sunday and ordered to leave.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: "We just had to throw our clothes on and come.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: We didn't know anything," one resident, who named herself only as Jo, said.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Another resident, Jason, said: "It all happened very quickly.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: We just packed our stuff up and came here." Several people in the leisure centre are still wearing their pyjamas, according to a BBC reporter there.

sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The prime minister urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts".
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast on Monday, Defence Secretary Wes Streeting thanked members of the public for their vigilance and quick action to alert emergency services to the plot.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: He added that the farmer who told the BBC about her 999 call "did the right thing" in reporting the men but said she only had a "partial picture", without expanding further.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The defence secretary said "this is not the time for me to speculate" over whether there was any Iranian involvement in the plot.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: On Iranian threats to the UK more generally, Streeting added: "We know that Iran and their proxies wish to do us harm." "In the dangerous and turbulent world we find ourselves in, investment in defence is a price worth paying," he added.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: The base was occupied by USAF Strategic Air Command during the Cold War and later the first Gulf War in 1991.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: B-52 bombers were also deployed by USAF from RAF Fairford on raids to Iraq in 2003.
sentences.article_title: What we know about RAF Fairford counter-terror probe

sentences.text: It was most recently used on 1 March, following a decision by former UK prime minister Sir Keir Starmer to allow the US to use UK bases - including RAF Fairford - for "defensive" strikes on Iranian capabilities.

sentences.text: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die The empty building that used to be the home of Marks & Spencer in Aberdeen is one of the first things you see when you arrive off the train and come into the city centre.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: The sign has gone, though the shape of the lettering can still be made out; the windows are blacked out and the doors boarded up.

sentences.text: As a teenager, I spent hours on Union Street, its main thoroughfare, nicknamed the Granite Mile after the local silver-grey stone.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: It was the place to try on all the latest fashions from the likes of Clockhouse and Chelsea Girl.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: The street used to be packed with shoppers from across the north-east of Scotland.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: "I come to Union Street to take a bus somewhere else... there's nothing to shop for now… it's horrendous," complains Marie Sim, a lifelong Aberdeen resident.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: It's a similar story across the country: High Streets, once bursting with shops, hit first by the rise of out-of-town retail centres and then by online commerce.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: But Aberdeen is in the thick of an ambitious turnaround plan.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: The Marks & Spencer flagship store in Aberdeen closed in August, 80 years after it opened there On top of that, the council is pouring tens of millions into trying to make the city centre a destination again.
sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: Like many other places, it's leaning into the "experience economy", with a new indoor food and drink market and a major redevelopment of the seafront.

sentences.article_title: My hometown shows that high streets have to change or die

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: 'I take my pillow everywhere': An expert's guide to finding your perfect match

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.

sentences.text: Paul Gorton believes he was targeted after sharing his holiday snaps on social media Traitors star Paul Gorton did not think twice about sharing photographs on social media while enjoying a family holiday with his wife and two young children.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: But when he returned home he discovered that his house in Cheshire had been burgled just days earlier.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "The eerie bit is at 21:10 BST I posted that me and Kate were by the side of the pool, we've got full bellies, the kids are in bed, we're actually having our little bit of the holiday," he said.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "About 20 minutes later, little did we know, our house has been broken into." Paul's bike as well as several sentimental items including an irreplaceable ring from Kate's grandmother were stolen in the burglary on 28 August.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: The perpetrators managed to break in through the bi-fold doors at the back of the house by using a technique known as lock snapping before cutting the broadband connection.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: Paul's home in Cheshire was targeted while he was on holiday Paul, who was a contestant on the second series of the popular BBC series, said he reported the burglary to Cheshire Police, with the force describing it as a "one-off hit".
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: As a result, Paul believes it was a "targeted attack".
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "They said they normally see people come in from far and wide and they [target] a couple of houses in a night but this isn't the case," said Paul, who is originally from St Helens.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "This makes me suspect that it could be someone that follows me.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "They've seen that I've posted that I was away and then thought 'let's go in the house and see if we can get ourselves some goodies'." Paul said he hoped other people would learn from his misfortune.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "I think the key message is for people to be a little bit smarter, more conscientious when they're posting and post when they're back at home.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "Hopefully people can learn from my mistakes.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: They were able to identify seven home addresses by using publicly available information.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: The fastest home address was identified in 15 minutes, with the first lead found in only 50 seconds.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "It's not just about social media," said Paul.
sentences.article_title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos

sentences.text: "I've learned to think about the whole picture with locks, alarms, lights, what you're posting online and whether you're accidentally advertising that nobody's home." Cheshire Police confirmed investigations were ongoing into the burglary but no arrests had been made.

sentences.text: OpenAI has been at the centre of new concerns over uncontrolled AI activity OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: AI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions", including the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Census Bureau and Education Department, the company said.

sentences.text: The disclosures come days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had breached non-public files on the website of its government-run health care scheme.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: Since August, public fears have grown over the potentially serious, even life-threatening, impacts of AI tools falling outside of human control.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites

sentences.text: OpenAI said that some of the data was accessed by AI agents, essentially bots that are designed and trained to operate somewhat autonomously, which were working to find "authoritative sources of public information".

sentences.text: But the company noted that some of the bots went beyond that and worked to bypass security measures on websites.

sentences.text: Nevertheless, OpenAI admitted: "This is not an appropriate use of this data." It added that the leak of user images occurred before it had put in place new safeguards on AI training, and it was working to get all the user images transferred to any third-party removed.

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: "Our approach is to pick small goals we aim to prove with flight data and we construct an airframe for that one task." The X-plane philosophy is to "minimise goals, the more goals you have the more expensive it gets." For the X-59 it's about suppressing sonic booms on a budget and nothing else.
sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.article_title: X-planes: Are they needed in the new era of drones?

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company Visit Toledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.

sentences.text: Fire crews hosed down an overheating tank in Los Angeles in May An industrial nightmare was brewing south of Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: In late May, a chemical storage tank with more than 7,000 gallons of toxic material began heating up – fast.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: The tank belonged to GKN Aerospace, a company that supplies parts to the aviation industry, including aircraft windows.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: As the temperature inside the shiny metal storage vessel rose, workers realised they had a problem.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: The tank was at risk of exploding, potentially showering nearby neighbourhoods with methyl methacrylate (MMA), a skin and lung-irritating , external compound used in plastics production.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: The tank's temperature reached 100F (38C) – though possibly went higher - 100F was simply the maximum reading , external on the temperature gauge inside.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: More than 50,000 residents of Garden Grove city were evacuated and fire crews began hosing down the tank in a bid to cool it.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: At one point, the vessel "actually bulged" according to the local fire chief.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Thankfully, no explosion occurred.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Months later, in August, GKN and local authorities announced a $100m (£74m) programme , external to compensate residents evacuated during the incident.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: But production of aircraft windows at the site, which had been halted, is still not fully restored.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Very few companies make aircraft windows This has sent a minor shockwave through the aircraft manufacturing industry because GKN is one of surprisingly few companies, anywhere in the world, that make aircraft windows – highly engineered, safety-critical parts for planes.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Production at GKN's Garden Grove facility currently remains hobbled, at roughly 50% of normal, according to public statements , external by its UK parent company Melrose Industries.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: The aim is to have full production restored by 28 September.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: GKN declined an interview with the BBC.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "They're one of only a handful of suppliers – less than a handful, really – of critical windows," says Marisa Garcia, an aviation industry analyst.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "We are supporting our supplier," a spokesman adds.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: An Airbus spokeswoman says, "We are closely monitoring and are seeing positive progress toward a return to normal." It comes at a time when airlines "can't get new aircraft fast enough," says Mike Stengel of AeroDynamic Advisory, a consultancy.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "They're holding on to aircraft for longer." Even though there are just a few aircraft window-manufacturing firms in existence, it's hard for new competitors to emerge because of how regulated the industry is, adds Stengel.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "It can take time to pivot to a new supplier." This leads to a "balancing act" between plane-makers and the firms they rely on for various parts, Stengel says.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Windows start with a sheet of acrylic To find out what goes into the making of an aircraft window, I spoke to Jean-Eric Vermont, general manager of French company Saint-Gobain Aerospace.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "We focus mostly on commercial aircraft, regional aircraft and helicopters," he says.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Vermont declines, though, to say how much market share his company has in aircraft windows – or transparencies, as they are known in the trade.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: The oval-shaped windows in the cabin, next to passengers' seats, are typically made of plastic-based materials, says Vermont.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "You start from a sheet of acrylic," he explains.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "Then you cut to size, [to] give the shape." A Saint-Gobain spokesman confirmed to the BBC that the company does not store or process MMA like GKN, but rather purchases sheets of polymerised MMA, or acrylic.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Aircraft manufacturers are increasingly ordering larger cabin windows, says Vermont, in order to offer passengers a wider view of the world outside.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: It's a selling point but it requires additional testing to ascertain whether the bigger windows hold up as well as the smaller ones.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Saint-Gobain tests its windows by exposing them to pressures many times what would be normal on an aircraft flying at altitude.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: These acrylic-based cabin windows are usually made out of two layers or plies, and Saint-Gobain also performs tests to confirm whether the window will survive even if one of those plies gets damaged.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: As aircraft windows get bigger, they get harder to manufacture Cockpit windows, Vermont says, are "totally different".
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: They are generally made of glass, which is chemically reinforced by adding potassium to it.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: This involves swapping smaller sodium ions for larger potassium ions, which helps to fill out the molecular structure of the glass, meaning that when it cools during production, it compresses into an extra strong, tight formation as it cools.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Some of the latest aircraft feature cockpit windows that are also curved, to make the plane more streamlined, which improves fuel efficiency.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: But curved cockpit windows are challenging to make – the slightest distortion or defect is clearly visible to the pilot.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: Quality control checks are used to ensure no such impediments exist in the final product.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "Typically, if you go through a hailstorm or if you hit a large enough bird, the external ply will crack," says Vermont.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "The cockpit window is designed for that." A London to Londonderry flight was recently affected by a cracked cockpit window .

sentences.text: While a mid-air emergency was declared, the plane landed safely.
sentences.article_title: The extreme engineering of aircraft windows

sentences.text: "There can be [such] cases," says Vermont, though he adds that Saint-Gobain's windows have not been involved in any recently.

sentences.text: Chinese firms dominate battery production Europe has taken some big swings in the battery industry in recent years and has made a couple of high-profile misses.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Both Sweden's Northvolt , external and Norway's Morrow , external filed for bankruptcy and there are fears in Europe that the continent has missed another technology shift.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: With more transport and industry switching from fossil fuels to electricity, batteries are likely to be a growth business.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: But the length of time required to bring new products to market, coupled with brutal competition, especially from China, means taking a substantial risk.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Could the answer lie at an almost unimaginably small scale?
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: An increasing number of investors and researchers think so.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: A single nanometre is one-billionth of a metre, but it's at that level that some of the most consequential work is being done.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "If you can make this work, it touches so many industries [but] it's a risky business," says Christian Rood, chief executive of Dutch tech firm LeydenJar.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Named after a 18th century precursor to electric cells, LeydenJar uses a technique known as plasma deposition to make a lighter, more efficient anode – an essential component of all batteries.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: Silicon is a highly effective and cheap material to use in anodes, but pure silicon expands and contracts as the battery operates and is recharged, which causes it to crack.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: However, using plasma deposition, LeydenJar can - layer by tiny layer - make an ultra-thin pure silicon foil which resists cracking, allowing a significant increase in battery life, charging speed, and energy density (up to 50%, according to LeydenJar).
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "Where normally a pure silicon anode would fall apart, [this] remains stable, so it was a very wonderful invention," says Rood.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "We address the bottleneck in the battery." LeydenJar's tech could mean better batteries Commercial-scale production will start at the end of 2026, but it has taken 10 years to get to this point – the very definition of the time and investment required for so-called Deep Tech innovations.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: It's no coincidence that LeydenJar's factory is in the Dutch city of Eindhoven - home to ASML and other important players in the computer chip industry.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "A lot of people talk theoretically about ecosystems; I can tell you this is one of our sources of competitive advantage," Rood says.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "It's really the crossover from semiconductors to batteries that makes us different - once you've demonstrated the principle in the lab, industrialization requires you to work with the semiconductor technology and suppliers.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: "That means a lot of risk, but also a lot of opportunity in terms of patenting, in terms of securing your whole intellectual property.
sentences.article_title: Can Europe recharge its battery industry?

sentences.text: And that's much more difficult to do in the US or in China." Across the Netherlands and Europe more widely there are multiple smaller Deep Tech start-ups looking to develop nanotechnology in the battery market.

sentences.text: The Conservatives have promised to prevent long-term jobless benefit claimants from spending their welfare payments on alcohol, cigarettes and gambling.

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: "The best welfare is a well-paid job.
sentences.article_title: Tories would prevent long-term jobless spending benefits on alcohol and cigarettes

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has branded a ban on fans being allowed to drink alcohol in the stands during men's football matches as "discrimination".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The prime minister told reporters that "I don't think it's fair for football fans to be singled out", as he suggested a change could be trialled.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Laws are in place which prevent drinking in view of the pitch at stadiums for clubs in the top five tiers of men's football in England.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Other sports do not face such a restriction.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The Football Supporters' Association (FSA) said the "outdated" legislation should be reviewed, but police chiefs have warned against relaxing the law and would like to meet the PM to "explain the challenges".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The legislation was introduced in 1985 by Margaret Thatcher's government for English and Welsh football grounds.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: At the time, then-Home Secretary Leon Brittan said that alcohol was a "major contributory factor in violent and disorderly behaviour" in football grounds.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Burnham is a keen football fan and a season-ticket holder at Premier League team Everton.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Shortly before he became prime minister, he criticised the restriction on football fans as he attended a rugby league game at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium where it was possible for supporters to have a drink in the stands.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Speaking to reporters on his trip to the United Nations in New York, Burnham was asked if it was still his view now he is in Downing Street.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: Burnham replied: "I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: There are different ways it could be done.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: It could happen on a trial basis.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "But I'm not going to back away from what's been a long held view of mine.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: I don't see how it can be fair that some supporters of one sport can be treated differently." Government sources have stressed that Burnham was restating an opinion that he has long held, rather than making any sort of policy announcement.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The prime minister's comments are not being seen inside government as an indication that he is looking to change the law in the area.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: A trial or pilot scheme to look at whether a change would be possible is not being ruled out but any wider move would require extensive consultation involving football clubs, fans and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport - none of which is currently planned.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: A UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) spokesman warned that changes to the law would pose "challenges" to policing and the "safety of staff and fans at football games".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: He said: "Other sports simply don't see the violence and criminal behaviour from their supporters that football does, albeit a minority, with alcohol often playing a significant part in violent and disorderly behaviour.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: "It would be irresponsible to fuel this by allowing greater alcohol consumption during games." He added it would be "incredibly rash to make fundamental changes without a full examination of the evidence and meaningful consultation with police practitioners who have the expertise in this area".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: FSA chairman Tom Greatrex said it was "unfair to criminalise football fans for having a pint while watching the match - especially since you can sit in the same seat drinking alcohol whilst watching an Oasis gig or rugby league".
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: He said "many clubs" were in favour of a change, adding: "We welcome the prime minister's comments and totally agree that the legislation is outdated and deserves to be reviewed." A fan-led review of football governance in 2021 called for the law to be re-examined.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The rules have been relaxed this season with all Women's Super League (WSL) clubs allowed to offer alcohol to supporters in the stands following two seasons of successful trials.
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: The law is more restrictive in Scotland, where the general sale of alcohol has been prohibited in Scottish football stadiums since 1981, but trial sales have been taking place recently and fans can now buy alcohol at Hampden Park games .
sentences.article_title: Burnham brands ban on football fans drinking alcohol in stands as 'discrimination'

sentences.text: This video can not be played The UK is reviewing its deal to hand over the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, the defence secretary has said.

sentences.text: Wes Streeting confirmed the deal was being looked at again after US President Donald Trump called it "terrible" at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: The original agreement would see the UK cede sovereignty of the territory to Mauritius and pay an average of £101m ($136m) per year to lease back a joint UK-US military base there, prized for its strategic location in the Indian Ocean.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: In April the deal, agreed under Sir Keir Starmer, was paused indefinitely because Trump pulled his support.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Streeting said "we have to" review the deal "because the United States doesn't support it".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: "What President Trump said yesterday wasn't new but I think it does provide absolute clarity that his position on this Chagos deal as currently drafted is not changing," he told BBC Breakfast.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: "So we have to do more work with our American allies, with President Trump and his administration, to get the deal to a place where he can support it." Streeting said the focus now would be to secure a long-term certainty for the base on Diego Garcia, the Chagos archipelago's largest island.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: He said it had been the view of every UK prime minister since Boris Johnson that an ongoing legal process - as Mauritius argues it was illegally forced to give away the islands in 1965 to gain independence - risks the security of the base.

sentences.text: During Trump's first face-to-face meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the UN General Assembly in New York, the US president criticised the "terrible deal" and said the UK was "going to be looking" at it.

sentences.text: He later told broadcasters he has "inherited the situation and we need a resolution".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Burnham added: "It's critical to safeguard the future of the base, and that matters to us for security reasons, but also clearly to the United States as well.

sentences.text: The "review" is not expected to constitute a formal process operating to a specific timeframe.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: However Streeting's comments were notable for their explicit acknowledgement that without changes the deal is not going to attract Trump's support.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Prior to the pause in April, the UK and Mauritius had signed an agreement in May 2025 and a final draft of the bill to hand over sovereignty of the islands had not passed Parliament.

sentences.text: Under the terms of the deal agreed in 2025 , Britain would hand sovereignty over the archipelago to Mauritius but lease back the Diego Garcia base for 99 years, which the UK government said would be a net overall cost of £3.4bn.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: However, Sir Keir, who was then prime minister, came under heavy criticism from opponents who said the real cost of the deal could amount to £35bn, adjusting for inflation, and risked allowing China to establish a presence on the archipelago.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Trump, who originally backed the deal, has been a frequent critic of the move, previously branding it a "a blight on our great ally" and an "act of total weakness".

sentences.text: Reacting to the review, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch called on Burnham to "just scrap this terrible deal".
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said: "The Chagos deal is dead.
sentences.article_title: UK to review Chagos Islands deal over lack of US support, Streeting tells BBC

sentences.text: Thank God." In 2019, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) gave an advisory opinion that Britain's separation of the Chagos Islands from Mauritius was unlawful and stated the UK must end its administration as rapidly as possible.

sentences.text: While non-binding, the ICJ advisory opinion - which was endorsed by the United Nations General Assembly - emboldened Mauritian assertions of sovereignty and led to the UK opening negotiations in 2022 .

sentences.text: Twenty-year-old Anna-May manages on about five hours' sleep a night It's the start of university - you're already on your fourth themed night out of the week and have signed up for every quirky-sounding society your campus has to offer.

sentences.text: "Getting daylight early on in the day is really going to help to keep your body in check.

sentences.text: How you sleep at night starts with how you wake up in the morning." Sleep is essential to learning and absorbing information.

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity
