sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Then comes the Milky Way.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: At 11pm each night, the village switches off its lights, plunging Hanle into darkness as visitors scramble to photograph the now-brilliant galaxy.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "When people look through the telescope and capture a photo alongside the Milky Way, they experience immense joy.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: We also help them with their mobile phone settings so they can capture the Milky Way," Padma Chamchot says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: It often starts with helping one visitor take a picture and ends with a long queue.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women take pictures for their own social media too, comparing notes on the stars and other sights they captured that night.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women also point laser at the sky to help visitors spot stars visible to the naked eye But by day, life is more ordinary.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Hanle has few hotels and no resorts, so visitors mostly stay in family-run homestays, often extensions of their homes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Chamchot's family runs one too.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Taking care of guests, cooking meals, cleaning rooms, and managing household chores fills our day," she says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "From nine in the evening, we begin setting up the telescopes for the night's stargazing sessions." Their families' homestays remain the main income source, but the women earn about 25,000 rupees ($260; £193) a month from astronomy, charging 200 rupees a session.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Income dips during the harsh winter, when few tourists visit, but the earnings have given them greater financial independence: they no longer need to ask their parents for money.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "We can save our earnings and spend them on things we want - including new phones," Padma says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: For the astro-ambassadors, the transformation has been personal as much as financial.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Before taking on this work, we lacked confidence," they say.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: However, the growing popularity of Hanle comes with risks.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The same tourism that supports local livelihoods could also threaten the darkness that makes Hanle unique.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Rapid construction and rising tourism also poses a threat to Hanle's dark skies Visitor numbers have surged, fuelled partly by social media posts about Hanle's night skies and its location on the route to Umling La, which is among the world's highest motorable mountain passes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: But more tourists also mean more traffic, construction and artificial light - all threats to the darkness they come to see.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Sonam Jorphail, a senior engineer and head of outreach at the IAO, says tourism is creating jobs and driving development in Hanle, but growth must be managed to protect its dark skies.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "They bridge the gap between the science community and common people - locals and visitors," Jorphail adds.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: But longtime residents say Hanle's night sky is already changing.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Padma's father, Dhuntup Chamchot, in his 70s, remembers when the skies were even darker.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "Back then, when the weather was good, people would often sleep outdoors under the open sky," he says.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The young women often take their families stargazing too.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "We frequently show the night sky to our families through the telescope.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They enjoy looking at it now," says Yangdol, one of the astro-ambassadors.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: "If one of us takes even a single day off, the families ask why the telescope was not set up," she jokes.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: The women say they have no desire to leave Hanle or its dark skies.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: They hope for advanced training and better telescopes and eyepieces to enhance visitors' experience.
sentences.article_title: The young women guiding tourists through India's night sky

sentences.text: Four years ago, the equipment was unfamiliar; now, they are building a future around the stars.

sentences.text: Accounts from local experts revealed that wild elephants used more than 35 plants, many of which have known medicinal uses African elephants use dozens of different medicinal plants to treat themselves and their families when they are sick.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: This is the conclusion of a study which interviewed people who live and work alongside the elephants in the Mount Elgon region of Kenya.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: These particular animals have long intrigued scientists with their extraordinary behaviour - they are known as salt-mining elephants, because they go into caves  and scrape the rock with their tusks to extract minerals for their diet.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: This newly published research suggests that the same elephants use several different plant species in the forest for medicinal purposes.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: "This shows just how entangled our medicines are with the non-human world," Dr Freymann told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: The researchers say the forests are 'natural pharmacies' for the elephants The scientists collaborated with the conservation charity the Mount Elgon Foundation , external .
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: They interviewed local people, including wildlife scouts and community elders.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Accounts described elephants selecting particular plants when they seemed unwell, and mothers reportedly giving medicinal plant material to their calves.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: From this, the researchers concluded that the elephants use 35 different plant species, and that 25 of those are known locally to have medicinal uses.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Wild chimpanzees filmed using forest 'first aid' Wounded orangutan seen using plant as medicine The study, published in the journal Scientific Reports , external , did not name the interviewees - keeping participants anonymous so they felt free to share their stories.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Their accounts reveal some intriguing details.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: In one testimony, a wildlife scout described seeing elephants using a plant known as Angurweet "as medicine to give to babies".
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Angurweet is used as a remedy for ailments including stomach ache.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: The scout, who  described elephant mothers mixing it in their mouths - "removing the leaves and chewing it until smooth, along with the roots of some other trees".
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: He also recounted  that he had seen mothers mix this plant material with their own milk.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: "They give it to the babies, who chew on it themselves and spit out the solids".
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Professor Michael Huffman, a primatologist based in Japan, currently at Nagasaki University, said this particular account was "tantalising", but more evidence would be needed to prove that elephants provided bespoke medical treatment for their calves.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: The scientists have already embarked on gathering that evidence - giving the local wildlife experts they worked with cameras to record the behaviour they witness.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: They are also analysing plants that the elephants use - looking for new medicines that the elephants themselves may have discovered.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Another lead reearcher on the project, Dr Fabien Schultz from the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine in Hamburg, told BBC News: "Local knowledge has given us a map".
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: The earliest scientific accounts of elephants practicing "self-medication" date back to the early third century.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Roman author Claudius Aelian in his text De Natura Animalium (On the Nature of Animals) described an elephant that, after being wounded by spears and arrows, consumed flowers and oil from an olive tree.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: The elephant made a full recovery.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Centuries later, these scientists are delving into what we can learn from wildlife about the properties of plants in the forest habitats they evolved in.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: "WIth each new species studied, we have gained a greater understanding of our medicinal past." For Dr Freymann, the findings also contain a lesson for our future.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: "So many of the medicines we buy in a pharmacy were derived from compounds from trees, algae, from fungi, from coral reefs.
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: "It's a win-win for us to protect these forests and keep those natural pharmacies around... long enough that we can discover new natural products that could save us down the line."
sentences.article_title: Elephants use medicinal plants to treat themselves, researchers find

sentences.text: Nicola Irvine and Toby White have been reporting an oily substance bubbling up in the river for more than a year An oil-like substance has been bubbling up in the River Avon in Bristol for years and killing wildlife, according to local residents who have made regular reports to the Environment Agency (EA).
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Nicola Irvine, who lives in Crews Hole, said it had been like "pulling teeth" getting the EA to investigate the pollution since she contacted them in July 2025.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Her partner, Toby White, said: "It's hard to describe how bad the smell is - at times it's like you're living on a petrol station and you start getting headaches." The EA said it had already visited the site and was "continuing to investigate the source of contamination and its damage to the environment".
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: An EA spokesperson added: "While minor impacts have been found where the contamination has entered the watercourse, we have not found wider environmental effects downstream.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Irvine said she first noticed the oily substance leaving a rainbow film on the river's surface and a strong acrid smell in early 2025.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: She reported it to the EA in July that year when she believed it was bubbling up rather than coming from boats.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The EA first dismissed the substance as surface run-off but, after Irvine continued sending photos, including of dead wildlife, the investigation reopened in May this year.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "This stretch of the Avon used to regularly have 30 to 40 ducks, but now it's unusual to see more than a handful," she said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I have personally found dead fish, ducks and ducklings.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Irvine said the issue had been even worse during this summer's heatwaves, which had led to her being prescribed medication for migraines.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "It would all bubble up, the smell would be so strong, it would surround the whole house," she said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The EA said the pollution was a category three pollution incident because impacts were limited to the area where contamination enters the watercourse.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I cant believe that even with all the health concerns and the fact there are otters in this river as well, it's still deemed minor," Irvine said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: In 2022, a leaked internal EA report told staff to ignore lower-impact category three and four pollution reports because of limited funding to investigate.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I've been so frustrated with the EA," Irvine said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "It feels like pulling teeth trying to get any action from them." The EA is also investigating another incident nearby at Brislington Brook , where dead fish and eels, foam on the water and "an intense chemical smell" were reported by volunteers.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: The oily substance on the River Avon's surface in August 2025 Dominic Linnell, who walks his dog along the river every day, said he first noticed the issue more than two years ago.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "Two or three times a week, there's an awful chemical smell, and I see a huge oil slick that seems to bubble up from the bottom of the river," he said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "I've seen fish floating dead and ducks.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: There's a lot of wildlife along there, you get herons, so it's a real shame.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: "We all really care about the river, it's definitely killing wildlife and it's very unpleasant," he said.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Another local resident, Tristan Dhalla, said he had noticed the pollution ever since he moved to the area five years ago, and neighbours had even claimed the problem went back as far as a decade.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: Wessex Water said their investigation had found "no issues" with any of their assets, while the substance did not pass through their sewerage network.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: A Bristol City Council spokesperson said it was supporting the EA's investigation by providing information and records, while officers had visited the site last week.
sentences.article_title: Getting river pollution investigated like 'pulling teeth'

sentences.text: James Benwell says searching for fungi can turn an ordinary family walk into an outdoor adventure From fairytale toadstools to fungi that look like birds' nests, experts say some of Britain's most unusual mushrooms are beginning to emerge as autumn arrives.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Hidden in parks, woodlands and nature reserves, species ranging from the bright-red fly agaric to the rare red cage fungus can be found by anyone willing to slow down and take a closer look.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: For James Benwell, of the Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust, searching for fungi has become a way to explore the outdoors with his young son.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: He said mushroom spotting can transform an ordinary walk into an adventure, revealing colourful and unusual species that many people pass by without noticing.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Across the West Midlands, fungi enthusiasts have recorded everything from tiny bird's nest fungi in Birmingham city centre, to fly agaric mushrooms growing beneath woodland birch trees and a rare red cage fungus discovered in Cannon Hill Park.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Many species can go unnoticed among fallen leaves, rotting wood and the bases of trees, but Benwell said taking the time to look more closely opens up a hidden world.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "Every walk becomes interesting and exciting if you're exploring and if you're looking for new things," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Magpie inkcap mushrooms get their name from their black-and-white appearance, Benwell said With more than 15,000 species of fungi found in the UK, experts are encouraging people to photograph and record what they find, rather than pick them.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Interest in fungi has grown in recent years, according to Lucas Large, chairman of the West Midlands Fungus Group, who said the organisation regularly attracted newcomers to its activities and fungi forays.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Benwell added one of the attractions was the variety of shapes, colours and forms that can be discovered throughout autumn.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "Sometimes you've just got to look through the leaf litter a bit, and you'd be amazed at the colours and different shapes and sizes of mushrooms you can find when you do look," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: The fly agaric's distinctive red cap and white spots have made it one of the world's most recognisable mushrooms Among the most recognisable species is the fly agaric, , external the striking red mushroom covered in white spots that has become closely associated with folklore and popular culture.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Benwell described it as "the mushroom of fairy tales".
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "It's in Alice in Wonderland, it's in Super Mario Brothers...
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: It's everywhere as part of fairy tales and folklore," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "But there are still adults who've never seen it." The bright-red cage fungus attracts flies with its distinctive smell Other species offer equally unusual sights.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Bird's nest fungi resemble miniature nests complete with tiny eggs, while the rare red cage fungus forms a vivid crimson lattice structure.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: The latter was spotted in Birmingham's Cannon Hill Park last year, in what Benwell said was only the second recorded sighting of the species in Birmingham and the Black Country.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "UK-wide, you're only talking hundreds of records ever.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: It's not a common species at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Large said the red cage fungus also had another notable characteristic.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "It smells horrible," he said, explaining the fungus attracts flies which help spread its spores.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: After more than a decade studying fungi, Large said the rarest species he had seen in the region was the coral tooth fungus.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "It formed this enormous kind of white, coraloid fruiting body," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Bird's nest fungi get their name from their resemblance to tiny nests filled with eggs While the colourful displays may encourage people to learn more about fungi, experts are warning against assuming wild mushrooms are safe to eat.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Several species found in the UK can cause severe illness or death if consumed, including the death cap mushroom, which the Woodland Trust says is responsible for most fungus-related fatalities. , external Large said there was no foolproof shortcut to determining whether a mushroom was poisonous.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "The only way to do it is to know which one it is, or be sort of certain that you've got a particular species," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: Benwell agreed and said people without specialist knowledge should avoid picking wild mushrooms.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "There are mushrooms that will harm you, that will make you sick or even kill you in this country," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: When searching with his son, the pair follow a simple rule.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: "No licking, no picking, no kicking." For Benwell, that approach allows families to enjoy the excitement of discovery while ensuring the region's remarkable fungi can be appreciated by everyone who passes by.
sentences.article_title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks

sentences.text: The project will focus on Cornwall, Kent and the North Pennines A project is under way to try and help one of the UK's "most threatened" species of bumblebee.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: The Bumblebee Conservation Trust is leading a £907,000 three-year scheme alongside the University of Cambridge to recover the Moss carder species.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: It said the initiative would focus on landscapes across Cornwall's coastal grasslands, dunes and heathland as well as grazing marshes and sea walls in Kent and the upland fringe landscape of the North Pennines.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: During the project, the trust said it would work with landowners to trial "small-scale habitat interventions" to identify those which work well while gaining a better understanding of the species' behaviour and needs.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: More news stories for Cornwall Listen to the latest news for Cornwall Moss carder bumblebees are largely found in small, fragmented populations, according to the trust.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: It said it was distinctive with a velvety covering of ginger-yellow hairs across its body and no black hairs.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: The trust said habitat loss and fragmentation were likely to have a bigger impact on the Moss carder than many other species as it typically foraged closer to its nest than most other bumblebees.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: Tylan Berry, Natural England's species and nature recovery networks senior officer, said the Species Recovery Programme was helping "take practical action to halt species decline and support nature recovery across England".
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: Berry said the Moss carder was "one of England's most threatened pollinators".
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: "Projects like this demonstrate how targeted investment can support practical conservation action on the ground," he added.
sentences.article_title: Bumblebee project seeking to help rare species

sentences.text: Friends of the Lake District wants to plant 1,500 wildflower plants at land at Mazonwath A project to preserve vulnerable vegetation and wildlife will see hundreds of wildflower plants introduced to an upland hay meadow.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: Friends of the Lake District (Fold) wants to plant 1,500 wildflowers on land at Mazonwath, in Little Asby, Cumbria, to help reintroduce many native species lost through some farming practices.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the environmental charity said plant roots were good for moisture retention and soil health, with their texture playing a part in slowing the flow of overland water.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: They added: "Conservation work like this is really important to help our insects and birds have a home into the future." Fold is calling for volunteers to help join the planting efforts on 13 October and more information on how to join is available on the charity's website.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: The charity will be planting great burnet, bird's foot trefoil, black knapweed, cranesbills, oxeye daisy and vetches.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: The organisation is working with Cumbria Wildlife Trust as part of the Cumbria Seed Bank Project, which aims to reverse the decline of grassland habitats in the county.
sentences.article_title: Hundreds of wildflowers to be planted at meadow

sentences.text: Volunteers are needed for a planting event at Mazonwath next month The two-year project in partnership with Kew Millennium Seed Bank, aims to collect, store and sow seed from rare and declining grassland species that are found in Cumbria.

sentences.text: Britain's first astronaut Helen Sharman officially opened the John Dulcamara Space Flight Museum at Grizedale Observatory A new space flight museum has been opened at a Lake District observatory.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: Britain's first astronaut Helen Sharman visited Grizedale Observatory and Planetarium on Friday to officially open the John Dulcamara Space Flight Museum.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: The collection was donated by private collector John Dulcamara and includes a piece of the command module from the 1969 Apollo 11 - the first manned mission to land on the moon.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: Sharman said the collection was "extraordinary".
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: Grizedale Observatory near Ambleside, Cumbria, opened in May 2024, offering public access to telescopes, a planetarium and meteorite laboratory, as well as staging a dark skies festival and other events.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: The collection includes a piece of the command module from the 1969 Apollo 11 space flight Sharman, who became the first British person to visit space in 1991, said: "It's an extraordinary collection.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: We've got bits of Apollo 11, bits from the Russian space programme - it's just an amazing collection of artefacts from space flight history.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: "It tells its own story of space history, but also of the people that went and the items that were important to them.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: "For it to be on show now in this beautiful way, as part of Grizedale Observatory, what a coup for Cumbria." The museum contains a variety of pieces ranging from autographed photos and signatures of prominent people in space flight to parts of actual space craft.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: Dulcamara said he first started collecting the artefacts after he attended a shuttle launch in 1996 and kept the ticket.
sentences.article_title: Space museum launched by Britain's first astronaut

sentences.text: "That's what started my 30 year collection off," he said.

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith was the only South African to win a gold medal at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris Having ended a two-year exile from competitive swimming, South Africa's most successful Olympian Tatjana Smith has revealed she "lost the love" for her sport before stepping away from the pool in 2024.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The 29-year-old's decision to retire straight after the Paris Games came as a surprise, given she had just won 200m breaststroke gold in the French capital to add to her 100m title from Tokyo 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: But after two years away, which included several months in which she did not swim at all, Smith says she is now "free from the things that made me hate swimming".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "My whole life, I was kind of a robot towards swimming," she told Newsday on the BBC World Service.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "You're so zoned in, you're obsessed with something, so there isn't actually time for you to think about things outside of the pool that you potentially have a passion for.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think probably everyone would think that the timing [of retirement] was the worst.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Smith on retirement and becoming South Africa’s most decorated Olympian But despite making history for her country, Smith says financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, also contributed to her decision to retire.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The financial burden on any athlete is so tough," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I relied on my parents funding me until I broke the world record at the Olympics.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: And then, all of a sudden, now people are interested in maybe sponsoring you.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But the majority of sponsorships for athletes are based on performance.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: So then you have that pressure and expectation to always have to perform, otherwise you're not going to get paid.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think the financial side, and also being in a system where they're not really putting the athletes first, made it really difficult." Smith won her first Olympic title under her maiden name Schoenmaker, before changing her surname when she married sports agent Joel Smith in 2023.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: The marriage made her part of a wider South African sporting dynasty, given that her sister-in-law is Rachel Smith, who was married to Springboks captain Siya Kolisi before their split.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Tatjana Smith admits her own marriage changed the way she thought about her future.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Thinking about families as a woman, you have to time it perfectly, because if you're pregnant, it's not like you can still compete." While children are not yet part of her journey, Smith says working out what to do next was far from easy.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I definitely understand what athletes mean from the post-Olympic depression," said the 2023 200m breaststroke world champion, who also counts Commonwealth and African titles among her achievements.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was such an emptiness in my life, because my whole life revolved around swimming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I don't have to eat at a certain time, I don't have to sleep at a certain time, I don't have to think about travelling or not spending time with family anymore.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The world is so overwhelming.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's like, in which direction to go?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "It was definitely the toughest season that I had to go through.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I think it's probably why it's made me a stronger person." Smith married her husband Joel in November 2023 and says family life was one of the reasons behind her decision to retire Initially, Smith took on speaking engagements to pay the bills.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: She smiles when she admits: "I hate public speaking.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: I hate being in front of people." The same cannot be said of her love for competition.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Having returned to the pool in order to keep fit, she decided to have a crack at triathlon, something she describes as a "crazy idea".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "The training was so intense, and I was like, 'OK, I might as well just go back to swimming if I'm going to train this hard'," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Every time I went back to the swimming pool and I dived in, I was like, 'Yeah, this is a feeling that I really miss so much'.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I think slowly over the year and a half, I just realised 'Wow, I really do love swimming'." Having made her decision to come out of retirement, Smith now wants to freshen things up and "try something new".
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: That means a change to the 50m breaststroke, an event which has just been added to the Olympic schedule for the first time ahead of the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I thought, 'Why don't I try?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Why don't I give myself that challenge?
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Reinvent myself'," said Smith.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I always try and describe it to someone that maybe doesn't understand swimming; it's like a 400m runner and a 100m [runner].
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's two different body types, two different trainings, and that's where I'm going." It means she has more than halved her training volume, with three sessions a week instead of eight - a change she believes will help her retain her love for her sport and live a more balanced life.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I feel like I'm being so lazy because I used to do 12km per day and now the focus is on taking time to be as explosive as possible.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Now I'm doing 12km over a whole week.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I have 20 years of endurance in my pocket, but I can definitely see I don't have those fast twitch [muscle] fibres.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: It's a whole different way of teaching my body how to swim." Those initial 20 years in the pool left Smith feeling burned out.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: Now she says she has earned the right to do things on her terms.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "Swimming was an opportunity given to me by my parents and I believe I took it on full heartedly.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "But, for the first time, it's my decision whether I want to come back.
sentences.article_title: 'I lost my love for swimming' - Smith comes out of retirement

sentences.text: "I've achieved way more than I ever dreamed in my whole life, so I have nothing to prove." BBC African Sports Personality of the Year 2021: Tatjana Schoenmaker profile.

sentences.article_title: Is Burnham right to blame Russia for spreading online disinformation?
